messages.subject_clean: Exporting ggvis plot with grouped data
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

good to know that I'm not the only one with this problem:))

I have no solution, but I need just to download a plot by a user in
browser. This is already possible by using the gear icon, so I only
reused the following Javascript and associated it with onclick of my
link in Shiny:

var onDownloadGgvis = function(button) {
     var plot = ggvis.plots["name_of_my_ggvis_plot"];
     plot.setRenderer("canvas"); // because svg rendering does not work
for me
     plot.updateDownloadLink(button);
}

Meanwhile, the export_png() issue was reported as
https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/332 - thanks!

Best regards,
Stanislav

messages.subject: Making line color consistent when hovering over lines
messages.subject_clean: Making line color consistent when hovering over lines
messages.body_plain:
Hi,  I am interested in making some interactive line graphs and wondered if it's possible to make them in ggvis.

In this example I'm trying to somewhat replicate the following chart:

http://next.mlssoccer.com/standings/weekly

As you can see, when you hover over a line that line is shown specifically in color and the other lines fade.  I don't think this is possible in ggivs yet?     I would also be happy in just having each line thicken and keeping it's current color.

Here are some example data:

mydf <- structure(list(team1 = structure(c(4L, 1L, 4L, 2L, 4L, 3L, 1L,
2L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 4L, 2L, 4L, 3L, 4L, 2L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 3L,
2L), .Label = c("AX", "DU", "MP", "OS"), class = "factor"), matchno = c(1L,
1L, 2L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 4L,
6L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 6L, 6L, 6L), rank = c(1L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L,
3L, 4L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 4L, 3L, 2L, 3L,
2L, 4L)), .Names = c("team1", "matchno", "rank"), class = c("grouped_df",
"tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"), row.names = c(NA, -24L), vars = list(
    matchno), drop = TRUE, indices = list(c(0L, 1L, 3L, 5L),
    c(2L, 6L, 7L, 9L), c(4L, 8L, 10L, 11L), c(12L, 13L, 14L,
    16L), c(15L, 18L, 19L, 20L), c(17L, 21L, 22L, 23L)), group_sizes = c(4L,
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L), biggest_group_size = 4L, labels = structure(list(
    matchno = 1:6), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -6L
), .Names = "matchno", vars = list(matchno)))

mydf  %>%
  ggvis(~matchno,~rank, stroke = ~team1) %>%
  layer_points(size := 50, size.hover := 200, fill = ~team1) %>%
  layer_lines(stroke.hover := "red", strokeWidth.hover := 4, strokeWidth := 2) %>%
  add_axis("x", title="Match number",  subdivide = 0, values = seq(1, 6, by = 1), format="####") %>%
  add_axis("y", title="Rank", subdivide = 0, values = seq(1, 4, by = 1), format='####') %>%
  scale_numeric("y", reverse=TRUE)

So my questions would be:

1) is it possible to change stroke.hover such that it is not set to just one color "red" but will be the same color as the line that is hovered over (i.e. red, orange, green, blue)

2) is it possible to make the other lines more opaque if another line is hovered over?

3)  if one hovers over a line and then move the mouse over a data point the change in line thickness/color recedes back to the original line color and thickness.   Is it possible to keep the line thicker when a point on that line is hovered over?

Thank you !

James Curley

messages.subject: Legends from layer_boxplots() and layer_densities() do not respect factor levels as I expected
messages.subject_clean: Legends from layer_boxplots() and layer_densities() do not respect factor levels as I expected
messages.body_plain:
The following examples use the data frame EPIDURALF from the PASWR2 package.  The levels of the variable ease in EPIDURALF are alphabetical (Difficult, Easy, Impossible).  Similar ggplot2 code is given for how I expected the ggvis graphs to appear with respect to the legends.  Have I missed something with ggvis or is there a work around to get the legends to respect the levels of a factor?  (I am using ggvis 0.4)

library(PASWR2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggvis)
xtabs(~ease, data = EPIDURALF)
EPI <- EPIDURALF %>%
       mutate(BMI = kg/(cm/100)^2)
EPI$ease <- factor(EPI$ease, levels = c("Easy", "Difficult", "Impossible"))
head(EPI)
xtabs(~ease, data = EPI)
levels(EPI$ease)
#  levels in legend shown in proper order as expected.
EPI %>%
  ggvis(~cm, ~kg, fill = ~ease) %>%
  layer_points() %>%
  group_by(ease) %>%
  layer_model_predictions(formula = kg ~ cm, model = "lm", se = TRUE)
# layer_boxplots() does not show levels of factor in proper order in legend (shows them alphabetically)
EPI %>%
  ggvis(~ease, ~BMI) %>%
  layer_boxplots()
# I would expect it to respect the levels of the factor as does ggplot2 below (Easy, Difficult, Impossible)
ggplot(data = EPI, aes(x = ease, y = BMI)) + geom_boxplot()
# Legend does not respect levels of factor ease for layer_densities().
EPI %>%
 group_by(ease) %>%
 ggvis(~BMI, fill = ~ease) %>%
 layer_densities(stroke = ~ease, fill = ~ease)
# I would expect the legend to appear as below (Easy, Difficult, Impossible)
ggplot(data = EPI, aes(x = BMI, fill = ease)) + geom_density(alpha = 0.2) + theme_bw()

# TIA

messages.subject: How to plot a histogram with Density instead of Count on the y-axis?
messages.subject_clean: How to plot a histogram with Density instead of Count on the y-axis?
messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to tell ggvis to display density (count / length of the var) instead of count when plotting a histogram?
In addition, how to overlay a density curve on top of the histogram?

For example, I've generated plot (attached) using the following ggplot2 commands.
How can I generate the same plot in ggvis?

library(ggplot2)

n = 100; p=0.5; mu=n*p; sigma=sqrt(n*p*(1-p))

# generate 5000 binomial rv's
r.binom = rbinom(5000, n, p)

# calculate the corresponding normal densities
p.norm = dnorm(r.binom, mu, sigma)

# combine into a data.frame
dat = data.frame(r.binom, p.norm)

ggplot(dat, aes(r.binom)) +
        geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), binwidth = 1,
                       fill = hcl(h = 195, l = 65, c = 100), color = "black") +
        geom_line(aes(y = p.norm),
                  color = hcl(h = 15, l = 65, c = 100), size = 1.2) +
        theme_bw()
